$comment: Gzip byte ceilings for scripts/check-size.mjs (esbuild bundle, production condition, min+gzip). Measured 2026-06-09: core-counter 5651 B, scaffold-counter 5754 B (audit's real vite-scaffold counter measured 7.10 KB). Ceilings = measured reality rounded up to the next 64 B; raise only deliberately, in the same PR as the growth. Headroom is deliberately small, so a raise is a decision rather than a drift. core-counter is set from its 2026-07-27 measurement of 6512 B, having accounted for all 781 B of growth over 63a896a commit by commit: 557 B bought Critical and High fixes (URL and handler sanitization, the compiled children protocol, Suspense, hydration and redirect correctness), 18 B was a signal-write perf trade, and the other 206 B is esbuild alone declining to tree-shake Suspense and ErrorBoundary past their _deferChildren markers, which Rollup drops. From 2026-11-20 the gate measures What's production tier (__DEV__ folded to false, see packages/core/src/env.js) and ceilings are the measured size plus at least 32 B, rounded up to the next 64 B: 32-95 B of headroom, which absorbs zlib differences between Node versions and nothing else.

core-counter.$raise-2026-08-15: 6528 -> 6592 for the 0.12.4 correctness release. Measured 6529 B, i.e. it went over by ONE byte, so the ceiling moves to the next 64 B boundary as the convention above requires. Growth over the 6512 B baseline is 17 B, against 1836 changed lines of packages/core/src. Almost all of that release tree-shakes out of a counter app entirely (data.js, form.js, a11y.js and animation.js are never reached by an app that imports signal/h/mount), so the residue is the code every app pulls in: spread() gaining the `ref` case it was missing, the boundary branches in hydrateNode, and flushScheduler re-arming a frame when a callback schedules work during a flush. 17 B for a release that closes a validation library failing open and a hydration path that duplicated nodes is a trade worth making explicitly.
core-counter.$raise-2026-08-28: 6592 -> 6656 for the conditional-list teardown fix. Measured 6631 B, so the ceiling moves to the next 64 B boundary as the convention above requires. Growth over the 6592 B ceiling is 39 B and over the 6549 B measurement 82 B, all of it in dom.js: the start marker that brackets an embedded list, and _liveRegionNodes, which walks that bracket when a region is torn down. The render.js half of the fix costs a counter app nothing, because the hydrate path tree-shakes out of one. What the 82 B buys is a region that removes the list it is holding: before it, hiding a conditional whose list had grown left every row added since mount in the page, and showing it again rendered a second list beside the orphans, permanently. There is no cheaper way to describe content that manages itself than a pair of markers, since a list of nodes is stale the moment the inner effect runs again.
core-counter.description: what-core runtime imported by a typical h()-based counter app (production condition)
core-counter.$change-2026-11-20: 6656 -> 6912 for the production tier and the new signal engine together. Measured 6840 B. The production tier alone took this scenario from 6601 B to 5729 B (-872 B: every development branch, warning text and the devtools pre-install buffer gone). The new engine (push-pull marking with linked edges, equality cut-off, cached errors, bounded-stack evaluation, two effect phases, O(1) owner unlinking) then adds 1111 B: the engine is 2532 B gzip for signal+computed+effect+batch against 1603 B for the old one with the same flag folding. Net +239 B over the old measurement, for an engine that completes all 20 reactivity workloads (13 before), never runs a node twice per write, and sets up a list row's reactive state in half the time (engine only, measured in Node).
core-counter.$change-2026-11-20-wave1: 6912 -> 7744 when the four wave-1 lanes (engine, client, server, diagnostics) were merged. Measured 7670 B. The merged tree measured 7573 B before integration, 733 B over the engine lane's own 6840 B; that growth has not been attributed lane by lane. Integration then added 63 B for reactive regions owning what they render, which fixes a removed row staying reachable from the mount root and the effects of a component built by a region re-run never being disposed, and 34 B for the ERR_NO_VNODE_RENDERER code on the compiled-runtime error. Every app resolving the production dist also carries the vnode renderer, boundaries and portal, because the single shared dist chunk keeps the renderer's install call (see compiled-counter).
core-counter.$change-2026-11-20-wave2: 7744 -> 8768 when the wave-2 lanes (API and packaging, client runtime, server, diagnostics) and the engine review fixes were merged. Measured 8721 B. The per-module production dist and no module-scope work in what-core (packages/core/test/module-scope.test.js) took this scenario from 7670 B to 7296 B on their own: h.js installs the vnode renderer only where a vnode producer is kept, a11y.js registers its focusin listener on the first useFocus() call, dom.js no longer registers the component lookup with components.js and helpers.js, and the inert server response and the rest of the shared chunk are gone; this h()-based app still makes vnodes, so it keeps the renderer. The client fixes add about 720 B on the h() path every h() app carries: 434 B for keyed vnode rows (a reactive child returning keyed vnodes, and the runtime <For>, keeps the row of every key that persists instead of rebuilding every row on every change; a small key matcher of its own, not the compiled lists' reconciler, which cost 2.6 KB here when shared), 195 B for class and classList composing in prop order under updates and classList function entries being reactive, and about 100 B for delegated events (the slotted-target retargeting, an element root running its own handler, target and currentTarget restored when a handler throws) and refusing outerHTML on every prop path. The engine review fixes add about 680 B: unlinking that is safe during the dependency walk, a loop cap that leaves the graph consistent, complete disposal of a node disposed during its own run, unobserved computeds releasing their dependencies, amortized O(1) explicit disposal, the ERR_COMPUTED_CYCLE throw and createSelector on an engine primitive. sig.mutate() adds 34 B, less 15 B for creating the signal and computed prototypes on first use. The engine's coded reports (ERR_INFINITE_EFFECT, ERR_SIGNAL_WRITE_IN_COMPUTED, ERR_NESTED_FLUSH_SYNC) are development-only and add nothing here.
core-counter.$change-2026-11-20-wave3: 8768 -> 8448 when ownership moved onto the owner tree. Measured 8415 B, 306 B under the 8721 B wave-2 measurement: components are owners of the engine, so the component stack and its per-component bookkeeping, the comment-to-context WeakMap, disposeTree and every DOM walk that existed to find reactive work, the per-insert owner capture and re-push, the _walk row flag, the region content scopes, el._propEffects and the hydration disposer registry are gone; what came in is effect- and computed-scoped ownership in the engine, error and pending handlers on owners, the mount root registry and user-phase useEffect/onMount. Ceiling per the convention above. Measured 8414 B with the wave-3 documentation lane merged on top (its runtime changes are development-only); ceiling unchanged.
core-counter.$change-2026-11-20-async: 8448 -> 8512 for async values (docs/ASYNC.md). Measured 8453 B, 38 B over the 8415 B wave-3 measurement: the engine hooks compiled-counter's async note lists, including the computed() dispatch. The async machinery itself is installed by the first computed() and is not in this app. Ceiling per the convention above.
core-counter.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 8710 B when the wave-4 async and hydration lanes were merged and integrated, +296 B against the 8414 B wave-3 measurement. Per lane: async values +38 B (the engine hooks compiled-counter's async note lists), hydration -56 B (the vnode brand and the hydration code no counter reaches). Integration, from ablation builds: about 190 B for keyed vnode rows following an item replaced under the same key (render.js sameVNode: a kept key whose new vnode renders other data gets a row built from it, and the reconciler of an h() app always carries it), and about 110 B for recognising vnodes another installed copy of what-core made (vnode-renderer.js: each copy registers its brand check under a registered symbol, so an app that ends up with two copies still renders their vnodes). The remaining 13 B are not itemised. Ceiling per the convention above.

scaffold-counter.description: create-what vanilla template counter (src/main.jsx equivalent) via what-framework + runtime JSX (production condition). Measured 8764 B on 2026-11-20 with the wave-2 lanes and the engine review fixes merged: 7332 B for the per-module dist alone (7713 B with the single shared chunk), then the same h()-path growth from the client fixes (about 716 B) and the engine fixes as core-counter; ceiling per the convention above. Measured 8461 B (-303 B) when ownership moved onto the owner tree (see core-counter's wave-3 note), and 8457 B with the wave-3 documentation lane merged on top; ceiling per the convention above.
scaffold-counter.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 8752 B with the wave-4 lanes merged and integrated, +295 B against the 8457 B wave-3 measurement: the same changes as core-counter's wave-4 note (async +40 B and hydration -56 B per lane, sameVNode about 180 B, the cross-copy vnode brand about 108 B). Ceiling per the convention above.

compiled-counter.description: The same create-what counter built the way the scaffold builds it: a production vite build through what-compiler/vite, resolving the production dist. Measured 6554 B on 2026-11-20 with the wave-2 lanes and the engine review fixes merged; the same app built from source measures 6559 B, and check-size fails if the two drift apart by more than 2%. The per-module dist measured 5697 B alone (8338 B with the single shared chunk, because Rollup kept h.js's renderer install call and with it the renderer, the boundaries and the portal). The client fixes add about 149 B that compiled JSX now carries (the class-component bridge, so a class component works in a production bundle, and the hooks a region needs to reach keyed rows), the engine review fixes about 680 B, and sig.mutate about 25 B net of the prototypes created on first use. check-size also fails if this app carries the vnode renderer at all. Measured 6302 B (-252 B) when ownership moved onto the owner tree (see core-counter's wave-3 note), and 6302 B with the wave-3 documentation lane merged on top; ceiling per the convention above.
compiled-counter.$change-2026-11-20-async: 6336 -> 6464 for async values (docs/ASYNC.md). Measured 6393 B, 91 B over the 6302 B wave-3 measurement; about 21 B of it is the dispatch that keeps computed() fast: a computed made by computed() is run through the async machinery behind one flag test in updateComputed, instead of through a wrapper around its function, which made every evaluation of such a computed about 5-7% slower. The async machinery is installed by the first computed() and is not in this app; what it carries are the hooks the engine and the component renderer need so that it can be: a computed run that throws is offered to the async machinery first (a run that started a fetch, or read a value that is not ready, is not an error; about 14 B), an effect's first run and re-run that read a value that is not ready are held instead of failed (about 24 B), a component that throws is handed to whatever suspension installed (failComponent: retried in place once its promise settles; about 16 B), and a computed's change test treats a value after not-ready as news (about 8 B). Ablating those four gave the 6302 B app back before the dispatch was added.
compiled-counter.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 6285 B with the wave-4 lanes merged and integrated, -17 B against the 6302 B wave-3 measurement: async values +91 B (the async note above) and the hydration lane's -113 B. This app makes no vnode and has no list, so the integration's vnode and keyed-row changes add nothing here. Ceiling per the convention above.

compiled-h-counter.description: The compiled counter with one h() call, built like compiled-counter. Making a vnode brings in the vnode renderer, the boundaries and the portal, and check-size fails if this app does not carry the renderer: the other half of compiled-counter's gate. Measured 9565 B on 2026-11-20 with the wave-2 lanes and the engine review fixes merged (8151 B for the per-module dist alone, then the h()-path growth from the client fixes and the engine fixes, as core-counter); ceiling per the convention above. Measured 9182 B (-383 B) when ownership moved onto the owner tree (see core-counter's wave-3 note), and 9174 B with the wave-3 documentation lane merged on top; ceiling per the convention above.
compiled-h-counter.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 9456 B with the wave-4 lanes merged and integrated, +282 B against the 9174 B wave-3 measurement: async +37 B and hydration -64 B per lane, sameVNode about 190 B and the cross-copy vnode brand about 97 B (core-counter's wave-4 note); 22 B not itemised. Ceiling per the convention above.

hooks-app.description: A small app on hooks (useState, useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useContext), a store, a form (what-framework/form) and useLocalStorage (what-framework/dom), built through what-compiler/vite on the production dist, so development-only code those modules reach would show. Measured 12707 B on 2026-11-20 with the wave-2 lanes and the engine review fixes merged, 12713 B from source: 12166 B for the per-module dist alone (14141 B with the single shared chunk, which kept every module any app reached a statement of), about 89 B for the client fixes, and about 450 B for the engine review fixes and sig.mutate. Measured 12364 B (-343 B) when ownership moved onto the owner tree (see core-counter's wave-3 note), and 12360 B with the wave-3 documentation lane merged on top, whose version of this app reads store fields as values, as stores expose them; ceiling per the convention above.
hooks-app.$change-2026-11-20-async: 12416 -> 12544 for async values (docs/ASYNC.md). Measured 12491 B, 127 B over the 12364 B wave-3 measurement: the dispatch compiled-counter's note describes (about 21 B), the hooks compiled-counter carries for them (about 62 B), a computed read's single test for a failed or not-ready value (readFailed, about 19 B; useMemo and a store's derived values are engine computeds, and one that reads an async value must hold its readers), and the gate that holds onMount and useEffect under a <Suspense> until its content first shows (about 21 B). The async machinery itself is not in this app.
hooks-app.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 12792 B with the wave-4 lanes merged and integrated, +432 B against the 12360 B wave-3 measurement: async values +127 B (the async note above) and the hydration lane's -100 B, then, from ablation builds, about 300 B for the item cells of keyed list rows (reactive.js _rowItem, _readRowItem and _setRowItem, render.js renewItem: when the reconciler keeps a key whose item was replaced, the row's bindings read the new item, and a row that read its item as a value is built again from it). The keyed reconciler's swap path takes about 41 B more: it reads keys only where a row's item changed, and skips the pass that hands rows their new items when no row between the swapped pair got one (a swap of two rows among 1,000 read about 2,000 keys and made a second pass over the 998 rows between them). This app makes no vnode, so sameVNode and the vnode brand are not in it; about 64 B are not itemised. Ceiling per the convention above.

what-error.description: signal plus an `instanceof WhatError` check from the root entry (production condition). Measured 3253 B on 2026-11-20. Before the WhatError class stopped reading the error catalogue for a default severity it measured 16950 B, because the class kept all of ERROR_CODES; createWhatError() and classifyError() now fill severity, suggestion and codeExample from the entry. check-size also fails if this app carries the catalogue at all. Measured 3738 B (+485 B) when merged with ownership on the owner tree: all of it is reactive.js, the engine's owner machinery (effect- and computed-scoped ownership, error and pending handlers on owners), which signal() alone already carries (3006 B before, 3491 B after); ceiling per the convention above.
what-error.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 3835 B with the wave-4 lanes merged and integrated, +97 B against the 3738 B wave-3 measurement, all of it reactive.js: the async lane's hooks in the engine that signal() alone already carries (an effect's held first run, a computed run's offer to the async machinery). Ceiling per the convention above.

diagnostics-read.description: signal plus the root entry's diagnostics read API: getDiagnostics, subscribeDiagnostics and clearDiagnostics (production condition). Measured 3203 B on 2026-11-20. diagnostics.js imports getErrorDefinition only for report(), which bundlers drop when only the read API is imported; check-size fails if this app carries the error catalogue. Measured 3698 B (+495 B) when merged with ownership on the owner tree, all of it reactive.js as in what-error; ceiling per the convention above.
diagnostics-read.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 3793 B with the wave-4 lanes merged and integrated, +95 B against the 3698 B wave-3 measurement, all of it the async lane's reactive.js hooks as in what-error's wave-4 note (the async lane's own tree measures the same bytes). Ceiling per the convention above.

computed-counter.description: The compiled counter with one computed(), built like compiled-counter. computed() takes a function that may return a promise or an async iterable, and cannot know which until a run returns one, so an app that calls it carries the async core: runs that supersede and abort, landing, not-ready reads, held effects, pending(), a component suspending in place. Measured 8629 B on 2026-11-20 when async values landed, against 6485 B for the same app before (+2144 B). The transitions (installed by the first startTransition) and the server data channel (installed by the first server render or hydrate()) are not in it: carrying them took this app to about 10.1 KB. Ceiling per the convention above.
computed-counter.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 8534 B with the wave-4 lanes merged and integrated, -95 B against the 8629 B the async lane measured: the hydration lane's savings on the compiled path. This app has no list and makes no vnode. Ceiling per the convention above.

async-app.description: An app on async values (docs/ASYNC.md), built like compiled-counter: an async computed read under <Suspense> and <ErrorBoundary>, a page change with useTransition, and an add with useOptimistic and startTransition. It carries the vnode renderer, because <Suspense> and <ErrorBoundary> make vnodes. Measured 16228 B on 2026-11-20 when async values landed; ceiling per the convention above.
async-app.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 16836 B with the wave-4 lanes merged and integrated, +608 B against the 16228 B the async lane measured. From ablation builds: about 283 B for the item cells of keyed list rows (hooks-app's wave-4 note), about 170 B for keyed vnode rows following a replaced item (sameVNode; <Suspense> and <ErrorBoundary> make vnodes, so this app carries the vnode renderer), about 90 B for the cross-copy vnode brand (core-counter's wave-4 note), and about 41 B for the keyed reconciler's swap path (hooks-app's wave-4 note). The rest, about 25 B, is the hydration lane's vnode brand and the fallback of a concealed boundary built under the boundary's owner. Ceiling per the convention above.

compiled-hydrate.description: A compiled counter with a keyed list that hydrates a server-rendered page, built with what-compiler's hydratable option (what the Vite plugin chooses for a project that renders on the server). Measured 14747 B on 2026-11-20. The same app built without the option and started with mount() measures 8292 B, and the hydratable build started with mount() 14853 B: the hydration runtime (the cursor, text and element claims, regions, lists, keyed vnode rows, boundaries and their streaming resume, mismatch reports and recovery, the hydration data channel's owner paths and late swaps) is about 6.3 KB of every hydratable build, and none of an app built without the option. It carries no vnode renderer. 124 B of it make a claimed element's attributes exactly its template node's (a static attribute the server wrote otherwise, or another attribute in its place, no longer survives) and compare a subtree with no bindings against the template's, claiming it node by node, with a report per difference, when the server wrote it otherwise. Ceiling per the convention above.
compiled-hydrate.$change-2026-11-20-wave4: Measured 16752 B with the wave-4 lanes merged and integrated, +2005 B against the 14747 B the hydration lane measured. From ablation builds: hydrate() installs the async values' server data channel (hydration-data.js seeding and the engine's seed operations, about 1098 B in every hydrating app, so an async value or resource made while hydrating adopts the server's value); <Suspense> and <ErrorBoundary> hydrate onto the async boundary record (reveal, the effect gate, children kept mounted out of the document while the fallback stands in, a component that suspends while hydrating, the streamed resume), 1963 B against the lane's 1630 B of boundary code, so +333 B; adopted keyed rows get item cells (about 226 B, hooks-app's wave-4 note); the cross-copy vnode brand is about 100 B; the keyed reconciler's swap path about 42 B (hooks-app's wave-4 note). Keyed vnode rows adopted from server markup are now reached through the vnode renderer's slot, so this app no longer carries them (about -520 B). About 730 B are not itemised: the async engine on the hydrating path (a region's or a row's held first run keeps the server's nodes, a dropped boundary's pending work holds back mismatch reports) and markerless text regions adopting the server's text node. The boundary hydration is in every hydrating app because the walker dispatches to it statically; reaching it only from apps that use a boundary is for a later wave. Ceiling per the convention above.
